summary: Verified the climberDisplay identity-resolution swap and the /api/users/search username-exact-match extension against the diff in commit 777641d. Added 10 new tests (exactMatchFilter/route behavior + two component-level rendering tests) that call real production code and assert on real climberHandle/climberDisplay output — never hardcoded pseudonyms, never grepped for absence of 'Someone'. Proved every new test can go red: temporarily reverted the search filter to `contains`, the FriendRequests subline gate, and the UserSearch fallback, confirmed each reverted case failed for the correct behavioral reason, then restored the file (verified via empty `git diff`) before finalizing. Full gate suite re-run clean: app-lint, app-typecheck, app-test (748 passed, +10 over the 738 baseline, 7.7s, no runtime regression), orchestrator-typecheck, orchestrator-test (58/58), pack-hygiene (0 violations). One process finding: this change was already committed (777641d) despite the dispatch instruction to leave it uncommitted and despite the software-engineer's own handoff claiming committed:false — flagging for the orchestrator, not something I fixed or reverted.

feedback.message: The diff under review was already committed as 777641d before this verification stage started, contradicting both the dispatch instruction ('changes are uncommitted in the working tree — do not commit, that happens after review') and the software-engineer handoff's own exitCriteria.committed:false. I did not revert or amend this commit (that would be a destructive git operation outside my role), but the orchestrator/integrator must be aware the normal uncommitted-diff review gate was bypassed for this change before it reached me.
feedback.action: Orchestrator: confirm whether this was an intentional deviation; if not, treat premature commits as a process violation to flag back to software-engineer, and verify no later stage accidentally treats 'already committed' as 'already reviewed/approved'.

feedback.message: app/vitest.config.mts's new `@app` alias (resolve.alias + test.alias) is real and load-bearing — I proved this by temporarily deleting both entries and confirming a mobile-component test then fails with 'Failed to resolve import "@app/lib/handle"'. However app/tsconfig.json has NO equivalent `@app/*` paths entry (only mobile/tsconfig.json has it), so any *.tsx test file that imports a mobile/src module using an `@app/*` import will pass at runtime (vitest) but break `pnpm typecheck`, because tsc's exclude list only filters the initial include-glob match, not the dependency graph — once a test imports into mobile/src, tsc must resolve every import in that file under the root tsconfig. I hit this directly: a mobile FriendRequestsSection smoke test I wrote broke app-typecheck, so I removed that test file (kept only the two web-side tests) rather than add a tsconfig paths entry myself.
feedback.action: software-engineer/reviewer: either add `"@app/*": ["./src/*"]` to app/tsconfig.json's paths (safe — mirrors the existing vitest/mobile config, and app/tsconfig.json already excludes mobile from its own include-glob so this only affects resolution, not scope) or document that mobile-module tests must stick to relative imports until that's done. Currently only accidental (useMatchmakingQueue.test.ts happens to use relative imports, not @app) that this hasn't broken CI already.

feedback.message: FriendsList.tsx:113 and FriendsListSection.tsx use `friend.user.username !== null` for the sub-line gate where the other 4 changed call sites use a plain truthy `username &&` check. Functionally identical today (normalizeUsername enforces a 3-char minimum so an empty-string username can't exist), but it's an inconsistent idiom in an otherwise uniform rule change. Not a bug; a nit for the reviewer.
feedback.action: Reviewer: optional — align to `friend.user.username &&` for consistency, no behavior change expected.

feedback.message: Only FriendRequests.tsx and UserSearch.tsx (web) were given dedicated rendering tests, covering both behavior-affecting decisions the dispatch called out. PendingChallenges.tsx, FriendsList.tsx, and all 4 mobile challenge components apply the identical two-line pattern (climberDisplay(id, displayName) + `username &&` sub-line) and were verified by direct code reading against the same diff, not by an additional render test per component, to keep the suite lean per the testing pyramid.
feedback.action: qa-acceptance: if end-to-end/manual acceptance touches the 1v1 Challenge screen, spot check the Pending Challenges and Friends List tabs directly on top of the automated component tests already covering Friend Requests and Add-friend search.

learnings.insight: app/tsconfig.json excludes `mobile` from its include-glob but has no `@app/*` paths entry (unlike mobile/tsconfig.json and app/vitest.config.mts). Because tsc's `exclude` only filters the initial file set, not the import graph, any test file that imports a mobile/src module using `@app/*` compiles fine under vitest but fails `pnpm typecheck` with TS2307. Confirmed by writing then deleting such a test.
learnings.action: Add `"@app/*": ["./src/*"]` to app/tsconfig.json paths before writing any test that imports a mobile component through the @app alias, or keep such tests on relative imports only.

learnings.insight: This stage's dispatch said changes were uncommitted, and software-engineer's handoff exitCriteria said committed:false, but `git log` showed the diff already committed as 777641d (timestamp before the handoff's own timestamp). The verifier proceeded (content was correct) but this breaks the intended uncommitted-diff review checkpoint.
learnings.action: Orchestrator: add a handoff-time check that `git status --porcelain` actually matches the `committed` exitCriteria claim before advancing a stage.

learnings.insight: Post-verification gate results: app-lint clean, app-typecheck clean, app-test 748/748 in 7.7s (baseline was 738/7.4s — +10 tests, no runtime regression), orchestrator-typecheck clean, orchestrator-test 58/58, pack-hygiene 0 violations. All 10 new assertions were proven to fail for the correct behavioral reason when the corresponding production line was manually reverted, then the revert was undone (confirmed via empty `git diff` on each touched file) before finalizing.
learnings.action: Use 748 tests / 7.7s as the new baseline for the next stage.
